summary: All three phases delivered their stated objectives. Phase-01 deviated from the plan's technical arbitration by keeping the import-graph build in execute rather than moving it to preflight, justified by five pre-existing tests that explicitly guard the invariant that CLI baseline-register refusals must fire before graph construction. Phase-02 added an unplanned edit to cli/commands/baseline.ts, forced by the mandated Violation discriminated union making the prior expression ill-typed. Both deviations are recorded and justified in their respective handoffs. Phase-03 conforms fully with no deviations. No excluded scope was violated. All planned artifacts, tests, and documentation are present.

findings.message: Objective fully delivered: per-type dispatch, AnalysisCapabilities record, ScopeImportViolation discriminated union, requiredCapabilities, per-type module, fingerprint/diagnostics switch on kind, stub builders, resolvePackageDir on port and adapter. No new rule type introduced.

apps/steme/src/adapters/package-resolver/node-package-resolver.test.ts was planned as CREATE but already existed at the baseline commit; it was extended with resolvePackageDir cases instead. The test coverage is present and correct. Acknowledged in the handoff.

Boundary contract respected: evaluateRules receives a closed AnalysisCapabilities record and never touches ports, filesystem, or process.cwd(). Graph build and resolver creation remain in the audit module.

Plan arbitration specified that preflight builds the import graph as its last step and that AuditPreflight carries graph and capabilities. This was not followed: the graph build remained in execute. Reason: moving it to preflight broke five pre-existing tests (main.test.ts, three in preflight-ordering.e2e.test.ts, baseline-lifecycle.e2e.test.ts) that are deliberate regression guards for the ordering invariant. Justified and recorded in the handoff.

All promised tests present: inference.test.ts (renamed field, requiredCapabilities), evaluate-rules.test.ts (missing-capability err case), node-package-resolver.test.ts (resolvePackageDir cases), capability.test.ts (graph build in execute, existing cases unmodified).
Commit subject and body match the plan exactly.

Handoff covers all required content: exported names and paths, suite pass confirmation, and explicit recording of the preflight/execute deviation with the invariance constraint that any future relocation must satisfy.

attentionPoints: Graph build is in execute, not preflight: the plan's technical arbitration called for moving it to preflight, but five pre-existing tests guard the invariant that CLI baseline-register refusals fire before graph construction. Any future plan that wants to move this earlier must explicitly account for preflight-ordering.e2e.test.ts's control tests.

node-package-resolver.test.ts pre-existed at the baseline commit despite being planned as a new file; it was extended rather than created. The reconciliation table flags this as action-mismatch. No correctness concern, but tooling that diffs planned-vs-actual file actions will flag it.

The PACKAGE_SURFACE_001 self-audit test seeds unused concepts (core.composition, core.capabilities) in the app manifest to prevent other active rulepack rules from refusing the audit with a concept-not-declared error before PACKAGE_SURFACE_001 evaluates. Correct workaround, but a future reader may find the extra manifest fields surprising without context.
pointers: build-capabilities.ts splitPackageSpecifier: verify the subpath extraction for a scoped specifier with exactly two segments (e.g. @scope/name — subpath should be '.'); check the off-by-one on the join. Confirm via unit test in build-capabilities.test.ts.

self-audit.e2e.test.ts seeds concepts.core.composition and concepts.core.capabilities which are not the concepts exercised by the PACKAGE_SURFACE_001 test case — if CORE_ADAPTER_001 or CORE_COMPOSITION_001 rule logic changes and starts requiring different concept declarations, this fixture could start failing for unrelated reasons. Confirm the fixture is minimal-correct and comment the reason for the extra fields.
